Why do better safety features rarely drop accident rates as much as we expect? 

• Anti-lock brakes stop skids, giving engineers high hopes for safer roads.
• Drivers subconsciously sense the extra protection and relax their guard.
• People start tailgating 15% closer because their car feels bulletproof.
• The saved physical safety gets instantly spent on wilder driving habits.

Where else in life do you see safety nets making people take bigger risks?
